claims.text: The Z method within ab initio molecular dynamics can accurately predict melting temperature.
The Z method can predict entropy of fusion.
The Z method can predict enthalpy of fusion.
The Z method can predict volume change at the melting point.
The Z method significantly reduces computational cost relative to full free-energy thermodynamic integration.
The initial state is a perfect crystalline solid suitable for ab initio DFT simulation.
Under the proposed protocol, the solid superheats and spontaneously melts.
The simulations are performed in the constant-volume NVE ensemble.
At sufficiently high energy, the superheated solid becomes unstable.
The onset of melting is indicated by a rapid temperature drop.
The onset of melting is accompanied by a change in potential energy.
Superheating to an instability causes spontaneous melting in the Z-method trajectory.
Abrupt energy and temperature changes at the transition can be used to extract melting properties.
The resulting melting-property estimates will closely agree with full thermodynamic-integration results.
Full ab initio free-energy thermodynamic integration is highly accurate.
Full ab initio free-energy thermodynamic integration is computationally expensive.
The reliability of the Z method may be limited for materials with complex or non-ideal melting behavior.

contradictions.description: The system is described as being heated continuously until it melts while remaining in the NVE ensemble, in which total energy is conserved. This is only coherent if 'heating' means preparing separate trajectories at successively higher initial energies, which is not stated.
